summary: The candidate ran the tests, guessed the sweep file was the likely location, made a quick edit, and confirmed the suite passed — apparently landing on the correct fix, but did so almost entirely without narrating hypothesis, mechanism, or root-cause reasoning at any point. The session was thin on process signal despite a plausible successful outcome.

dimensions.analysis: The candidate never read the failing test body or the failure diff before diving into the sweep file. They went straight from a failed test run to poking around without articulating what the test expected or what ambiguity existed around partially-shipped holds.

The stated plan was only a location (the sweep file), never a mechanism. There was no hypothesis about the sweep releasing the wrong quantity, remaining vs original units, or any specific behavior being tested.

Aside from the initial vague intent to poke around and a closing remark that the test passed, there was no narration of what was read in sweep.ts, what was suspected, or what the edit actually changed. The 40-second gap between opening the file and editing it has no accompanying commentary explaining the reasoning.

The edit to sweep.ts and subsequent green test run suggest the fix landed on the correct location and likely addressed the actual root cause, but with no stated plan there is little to judge the edit against beyond the outcome itself.

They did re-run the test suite after the edit and confirmed a pass before ending the session, which is the minimum verification step, though no edge-case check (e.g. confirming full-release holds still behave correctly) was mentioned.

The closing statement is a bare acknowledgment that the suite passed, with no explanation of why the original bug existed (releasing original count instead of remaining count) or why the fix corrects it. No root-cause articulation was offered despite the opportunity at session end.
